_about: Formatting rules for Musicians' Club chord charts. One file read by both the renderer (src/chart) and the PDF importer (src/importers/pdf-chart). Change a rule here and both follow; neither tool's code needs to change. Keys starting with '_' are notes and are ignored. Sizes are in points (1/72 inch), US Letter. '(verify)' marks values to confirm with the owner.

legend._note: Colors of the Music Legend marks (CLAUDE.md section 5).

colors._beatRed: Beat-tag digits are a slightly different red in the files.
colors._blue: Dark blue: the first repeated riff's circled numbers (and the down arrow). The second riff uses light blue (render.riffColors).

render._note: How charts are drawn. Measured from the sample PDFs (mostly Since U Been Gone); drift between files noted.

page._bottomLimit: Lowest y for a section's closing rule. SUBG page 2 ends with content at 768.6 and its rule just below; the footer baseline is 789.1. (verify)
page._targetPages: Charts aim to fit this many pages (owner); more prints a warning.

squish._note: When a chart would run past page.targetPages, vertical spacing is tightened from the max (row.height, section padding) just enough to fit, down to these minimums (owner, 2026-11-09: keep sections whole; squish section height to stay on 2 pages; rows between 17 and 20 pt). Font sizes and notation images never shrink. The minimum row height keeps a chord's superscript clear of the lyric descenders above it at arm's length. (verify)

colors._lyricUpright: '{2. I get}' text inside an ending in the lyric line.
colors._noBass: Gray chord = no bass (Legend **). Not measured separately; lyric gray. (verify)

render._repeatColors: Colors for repeated sections, in priority order (owner, 2026-11-08): the first repeated section from the top of the chart is blue, the second green, the third purple (the font colors in Awitin Mo At Isasayaw Ko). A label is colored only when a later 'Repeat ...' line points back to its section; other labels print black, regular. A fourth repeated section reuses purple, with a warning.

header._dateSize: Date, Calibri 10, at the left margin.
header._titleCenter: 'TITLE' Calibri Bold 18 then ' (Artist, Year)' Calibri 14, centered as one block on x = 295.3 (all five sample PDFs agree to 0.1 pt; not the page center).

rule._x1: Section rules run nearly edge to edge (5.8 to 606.4 pt).
rule._firstY: First rule, under the header (every page, including pages without a header).

section._labelX: Label column: Arial 9 at the left margin. Awitin uses 11 pt; 9 pt chosen (most files).
section._ordinalSize: Ordinal suffix ('st' in '1st Ver'): 6 pt, raised 3 pt.
section._padTop: First baseline = rule + this (SUBG: 16.4-16.6 pt). Rows start at rule + padTop.
section._padBottom: Rule = last row bottom + this (SUBG: last baseline + 10.3).
section._labelBaselineOverSnippet: When a section starts with a snippet, its label (and the overlay text) sit 10 pt below the rule.

row._height: Row height (chord line and lyric line are each one row of 16 pt text) and the MAX row height: used whenever the chart has room (owner, 2026-11-09: max 20 pt, always used when space allows). The original charts measure 18.4 pt. Tightened toward squish.minRowHeight only when that keeps the chart within page.targetPages.
row._baseline: Baseline below the row top. Keeps the measured 3.7 pt below the baseline for descenders (18.4 - 14.7), so baseline = height - 3.7.

chord._extensionWeight: Weight of a chord's extension (everything after root, flat/sharp and minor 'm'), taken as one unit at its own middle, relative to one core symbol. Used to find the chord's beat point. The owner (2026-11-09) said extensions count for less but was unsure how much. (verify)
chord._bassWeight: Weight of a slash bass ('/F#') as one unit at its own middle. Owner (2026-11-09): less than an extension, but not nothing. (verify)
chord._accidentalSize: Flat/sharp after the root: 12 pt in the files ('B' 16 + 'b' 12).
chord._supSize: Quality and beat tags: 10.6 pt superscript, raised 5.5 pt.
chord._bassSize: Slash bass: '/F' 14 pt, its accidental 11 pt.
chord._glyphScale: Symbol outlines at this multiple of the run size (same rule as diagrams).
chord._slashTuck: Slash tucked under a preceding superscript, as on the cover diagrams (owner, 2026-11-08). Computed from the Arimo outlines at chart sizes: untucked, the slash is 4.45 pt from a superscript '7' and 2.96 pt from a ')'; these leave about 2 pt in both cases, the diagrams' clearance scaled to a 16 pt root.

render._riffColors: Riff-reference colors by riff (owner, 2026-11-08): first repeated riff dark, second light.

marks._size: Bar lines, '-', stops and braces: 16 pt like the chords.
marks._endingNumberSize: Repeat-ending number '1.' in braces: Arial Bold 9.
marks._meterSize: Stacked meter digits (an image in the files, about 7 x 17 pt). (verify)

note._size: 'Repeat ' Arial 12 then the section name Arial Bold 16 in its color.

spacing._groupGap: Minimum gap between two chord-line groups: one 16 pt space.
spacing._itemGap: Gap between items in a group, except next to bar lines and stops.
spacing._tabOrigin: Word's default tab stops: every 0.5 inch from the 0.1 inch margin (so 0.6 inch is a stop). Untimed chords past the end of the lyric go on this grid (owner, 2026-11-08).
spacing._timingNear: 'before'/'after' chords: distance to the syllable they belong to (near) and to the other side of the gap (far). The asymmetry shows the timing. (verify)
spacing._beatWidth: Rhythm spacing: points per beat for timed chords and syllables (owner, 2026-11-09). A beat sits at the middle of its syllable and the weighted middle of its chord; points are pushed right when text would collide, and later points keep their proportional distance. Measured: lyric entries at about 26 pt (beat 2), 50.4 pt (beat 3), 79 pt (beat 4), 11.6-16 pt (beat 1&) in Since U Been Gone, 21.6 / 43.2 pt in American Boy and So Easy; full chord lines run 25-28 pt per beat. Lines that don't fit flex this down first (see fitLine). (verify)
spacing._hyphenPad: Space on each side of the hyphen in a word split by a gap ('start - ed').

render._narrowScale: Arial Narrow is about 82% of Arial's width (measured 0.81-0.82). Lines are compressed down to this before they wrap.

cover._note: Cover pages (CLAUDE.md §2 item 2, §4.3). Measured from Word's PDF export of the four templates in samples/ (6 col; 8 col page 1; 8 col page 2 with chords and Legend; 8 col page 2 Legend only). The filled covers (24K Magic, Mad World) are not in the repo yet: values marked (verify) are to be checked against them.
cover._logo: Club logo, 177.5 x 86.5 pt, centered, with Word's soft drop shadow (black at 40%, 3 pt down-right, 4 pt blur). logoY values are the logo's top.

header._note: Page 1 top: logo, a dark blue rule, the title, a second rule, then 'Artist, Year (Key of X, Original)'. The 8-column template sits 4.6 pt higher and starts its panel 20.8 pt higher than the 6-column one, to make room for 7 rows at 65%; both are kept as measured.
header._center: Title and subtitle are centered on the page. (verify: Word's centering includes a trailing space, about 3 pt)
header._maxWidth: A title or subtitle wider than this is narrowed (fonts never shrink below narrowScale of their width; a warning is printed past that). (verify)

panel._note: A panel is a dark blue header bar ('CHORDS:', 'LEGEND:') over a body box outlined in light blue. Header heights vary between templates (24.4 to 34.1 pt); one height is used.

layouts._note: Panel boxes [x0, x1] and body bottoms. 'beside': chords with the Legend beside them on page 1 (6-column template). 'full': chords across page 1, Legend on page 2 (8-column template). 'continued': page 2 with 'CHORDS (con't.)' and the Legend. 'legendOnly': page 2 with only the Legend. Page 2 templates use 0.5 in side margins, page 1 0.2 in; kept as measured. (verify)

columns._note: Column count is chosen by diagram count (owner, 2026-11-09): the fewest that fit, starting from the default of 5; 4 when that leaves fewer empty places in the last row (even use of white space). Each count uses the largest scale (in steps) that fits its panel width and the diagrams; 4 replaces 5 only at its full width scale (otherwise its gaps would be uneven). 4 to 6 columns sit beside the Legend; 7 and 8 use the full width and move the Legend to page 2.
columns._scales: Allowed scales. The templates show 60% at 6 columns and 65% at 8; with the gaps below, the panel widths give 90% at 4, 70% at 5 and 75% at 7. (verify 4, 5, 7 against their templates)
columns._hgapMin: Smallest space between two diagrams in a row; the rest of the width is spread evenly.
columns._maxRows: Rows per panel, as written in the templates (6x7=42, 8x7=56, 4x5=20 on page 2).

chords._tuning: Tuning label, e.g. 'Eb Standard Tuning': Calibri Bold Italic 13, red, top left of the chords panel.
chords._top: First diagram top below the panel body top, with and without a tuning label.
chords._padX: Space between the panel outline and the outer diagrams (their boxes have their own white margins).
chords._note: Per-diagram note, e.g. 'for Bridge only': Calibri Italic 11, red, centered under its diagram; a row with a note is this much taller.
chords._alternate: 'Alternate (for Acoustic):' group: a double rule, then the label (Calibri Italic 13, the part in parentheses red), then its diagrams on new rows.
chords._continued: 'Continued at back of page' (Calibri Bold Italic 13, red, centered) just under the last row when diagrams overflow to page 2. The 8x7 rows at 65% leave only about 8 pt under the last row, so the line sits close to it. (verify)

legend._note: The printed Music Legend. Which entries print, and their order, is checked against the registry (src/legend/registry.ts): every entry id must be a confirmed registry entry, and every confirmed entry must print. Markup: <r> red, <g> green, <b> bold, <i> italic, <sup> superscript, <big> 10 pt instead of 9; \n starts a new line.
legend._rule: Rule under the footnotes. (verify color and weight)

footnotes.text: *All chord changes occur at either the 1<sup>st</sup> or middle beat (i.e. 3<sup>rd</sup> beat in 4/4 time signature) when not shown.
**Gray colored chords mean do not play any Bass Guitar
***Lyrics sung by backup vocalists are indicated by italicized lyrics

entries.text:
- “<r>#</r>” indicates at what beat a chord changes (optional)
- “<r>&</r>” indicates 8<sup>th</sup> note intervals
- “<r>e</r>”, “<r>&</r>”, “<r>a</r>” indicates 16<sup>th</sup> note intervals
- “<r>te</r>”, “<r>ta</r>” indicates triplet note intervals
- on repeats, “<r>#</r>” indicates which time to play (1<sup>st</sup>, 2<sup>nd</sup>,… time)

<big>- abrupt stop</big> (when placed before a beat, end before that beat; if placed after a beat, end on that beat. When multiple beats are shown <sup>(<r>#,#</r>)</sup> more than one hit is required.)
<big>- stop and hold</big> (When multiple beats are shown <sup>(<r>#,#</r>)</sup> more than one hit is required.)
- passage of music played as many times as needed

footer._note: 'Musiciansclub.com' (Calibri Italic 11, link blue, underlined) and the date (Calibri 11). Not centered on the page in three of the four templates. (verify)

notation._note: Native notation (owner, 2026-11-09): MusicXML drawn by alphaTab, music symbols as Bravura outlines. Tab, standard or both, chosen per notation block.
notation._scale: alphaTab drawing scale. At 0.57 tab lines are about 7.4 pt apart, like the Cubase snippets in today's charts (SUBG: 6 tab lines over about 37 pt). (verify)
notation._gapBelow: Space between the bottom of the notation and the next row, pt.
notation._instrumentSize: Instrument label ('Lead') before the first chord name: small italic, like the snippets' 'Lead'.
notation._placeholderHeight: Height of the dashed box shown when a notation block can't be drawn and has no fallback image.

lyrics._note: Sung syllables (owner, 2026-11-09): a beat sits on the middle of its syllable, so multi-syllable words are split (Walk|ing). Hyphenation patterns per language (the 'hyphen' package), then a sung-syllable rule for short edge syllables (to|night, a|way) and for languages without patterns. See src/text/syllables.ts.
lyrics._defaultLanguage: Language of a chart's lyrics when meta.language is not set.
lyrics._patterns: Language -> hyphen pattern set. Languages not listed (e.g. Tagalog 'tl') use the sung-syllable rule alone.
lyrics._digraphs: Consonant pairs that sound as one in the sung-syllable rule: 'onset' pairs start the next syllable (fa|ther; Tagalog pa|nga|rap), 'coda' pairs end the syllable before (English sing|er, pick|ing). Per language, with a default.
lyrics._exceptions: Words the rules split wrongly, written with their sung syllables, e.g. 'fire' (one syllable) or 'fi-re' (two).

timing._defaultMeter: Meter when a chart does not set one (owner, 2026-11-09: 4/4).

sections._types: How a section label maps to a section type, tried in order (case-insensitive regular expressions). Used by the importer, and for 'Repeat ...' lines.
sections._repeatWord: Word that starts a 'Repeat Chorus' line.

symbols._note: Vocabulary of the chord line, from the Music Legend and the marks used in today's charts.
symbols._stopColors: Color of '//' -> stop kind (Legend: red abrupt stop, green stop and hold).
symbols._instrumentOps: Sign before an instrument inside parentheses -> op. '⊕'/'⊗' are tiny images in the Word PDFs (see import.circledOps).
symbols._instrumentJoin: Several instruments in one mark, e.g. '(+Bss/Drm)'.
symbols._refGlyphs: Circled riff numbers 1-10 as Unicode (the Word PDFs use Wingdings U+F08C-U+F095 for the same).
symbols._minor: A quality starting with 'm' (but not 'maj') is minor; its 'm' counts in the chord's core weight.

import._note: How the legacy Word-made PDFs encode charts, for the PDF importer. These describe the old files, so they stay put when the drawing rules above change.
import._lyricColors: Gray lyric text (and gray 'no bass' chords).
import._ruleMinWidth: Section rules: filled bars at least this wide and at most ruleMaxHeight tall (gray #A6A6A6, black in Awitin).
import._headerMaxY: Header text sits above this baseline on page 1; footer text below footerMinY.
import._labelMaxX: Section label characters start left of this x (the content starts at 43.2; 'End Cho' reaches 40); label text is at most labelMaxSize pt.
import._mainSizeMin: Lyric and chord rows use 15-18 pt text; smaller text is superscript, aside, or a small mark.
import._superscriptRaise: A character whose baseline is at least this far above its row's baseline is a superscript (quality, beat tag, ordinal).
import._rowJoin: Small text within this distance above a main row belongs to that row.
import._rowPair: A chord row and the lyric row below it form one line when their baselines are at most this far apart.
import._wordGap: Gap (fraction of the font size) above which two characters are separate words.
import._syllableHyphens: A hyphen with space on both sides between two letters splits a sung word ('start - ed'); it is removed and the word joined.
import._bassSlashGap: A plain '/' then a root letter at most this far (pt) after a chord is its slash bass (hand-made files leave 0-9 pt).
import._groupGap: A gap wider than this (pt) between chord-line marks starts a new group; bars and chords always start one.
import._wingdingsRefStart: Wingdings code for circled 1 (U+F08C); circled n is this + n - 1.
import._circledOps: The circled plus/times before an instrument are tiny images no larger than this (pt).
import._snippetMinWidth: Images at least this wide are notation snippets.
import._legacyBeatWidth: Points per beat in the legacy charts: a late lyric starts about this far per beat after its line's opening bar line (measured on Since U Been Gone; American Boy and So Easy run 21.6). Separate from render.spacing.beatWidth so changing how we draw does not change how old files are read.
import._entryMinBeats: A lyric starting at least this many beats after its line's opening bar line gets a guessed lyricEntry.
import._rhythmGrid: Guessed beats are rounded to this fraction of a beat (0.5 = eighth notes).
import._betweenSyllables: A chord whose middle is farther than this (pt) outside the nearest syllable is placed 'before'/'after' it and flagged.
